title: Trace a discovery decision under failure
description: Choose how a workload reads the catalog, define what healthy means, then inject a failure. The lab keeps discovery freshness, check semantics, and traffic eligibility separate.

interfaces.label: Consul DNS
interfaces.detail: Low-friction service lookup through the local agent. DNS uses stale reads by default.
interfaces.healthyBehavior: Fast, scalable lookups without application-specific Consul API code.
interfaces.outageBehavior: A reachable follower can answer without a leader, but the result has no hard upper staleness bound.

interfaces.label: HTTP health API
interfaces.detail: Query the local agent for passing instances using the HTTP API's default consistency mode.
interfaces.healthyBehavior: Returns an authoritative-enough catalog view for most application discovery.
interfaces.outageBehavior: The request needs a leader path and can fail when the server quorum is unavailable.

interfaces.label: HTTP consistent read
interfaces.detail: Require the leader to verify its authority with a quorum before returning the catalog result.
interfaces.healthyBehavior: Provides the strongest catalog-read contract at the cost of another quorum round trip.
interfaces.outageBehavior: Unavailable without a leader and quorum; do not use it for every routine lookup by default.

interfaces.label: HTTP agent cache
interfaces.detail: Use a cache-capable endpoint with explicit max-age and stale-if-error behavior.
interfaces.healthyBehavior: Collapses repeated reads onto a local cache while a background query refreshes supported resources.
interfaces.outageBehavior: Can fail static from a warm cache; the Age header becomes part of the traffic-safety decision.

checks.label: HTTP readiness
checks.detail: Probe an application endpoint that verifies the process can accept useful work.
checks.detects: Application-level rejection, dependency policy, and bad HTTP status
checks.blindSpot: A shallow endpoint can still report passing while critical dependencies are unusable

checks.label: TCP reachability
checks.detail: Verify that a connection can be established to an address and port.
checks.detects: Closed port, refused connection, and basic network reachability failure
checks.blindSpot: A hung or logically unhealthy process may still accept TCP connections

checks.label: TTL heartbeat
checks.detail: Require the workload or an external controller to renew status before a deadline.
checks.detects: Missing heartbeat from a process that owns the liveness contract
checks.blindSpot: The check is only as truthful as the component that updates it

incidents.label: Healthy steady state
incidents.detail: The service is ready, the local agent can reach servers, and the server cluster has quorum.

http-readiness.explanation: The readiness endpoint accepts the probe and represents the intended traffic contract.

tcp-port.explanation: The port accepts a connection. In this scenario the process is also genuinely ready.

ttl-heartbeat.explanation: The workload renews its heartbeat before the TTL expires.

incidents.label: Process accepts TCP but is hung
incidents.detail: The socket still opens, but application requests cannot complete useful work.

http-readiness.explanation: A bounded readiness probe fails and removes the instance after the configured threshold.

tcp-port.explanation: The port accepts a connection, so a TCP-only check keeps an unsafe endpoint eligible.

ttl-heartbeat.explanation: If the application owns the heartbeat loop, the missing renewal turns the check critical after the TTL.

incidents.label: Consul servers lose quorum
incidents.detail: Client agents and some servers remain reachable, but the Raft peer set cannot elect or confirm a leader.

http-readiness.explanation: The last observed readiness result may still be served, but new catalog writes cannot commit.

tcp-port.explanation: A previously passing result can outlive the current control-plane observation window.

ttl-heartbeat.explanation: The workload may renew locally, but the authoritative catalog cannot commit updates without quorum.
